pitch_uk: Кожна кімната має один впізнаваний силует сливовим чорнилом на кремовій плитці, і той самий штамп стоїть на коробці, на дверях, на стійці місця доставки та на мапі.
angle: ground.md section 4, angle A: one code only, the silhouette. No colour per room, no frame shape per room, no 3D landmark.

grid.artboard: 64 x 64 units, live area 4..60 (56 units); viewBox 0 0 64 64
grid.minimum: every stroke, gap and counter is at least 6 units (2.25 px at 24 px, 1.4 px at 15 px); bars are 7 to 9 units; corner radius 3 to 6
grid.fill: filled silhouettes in one ink, counters cut out (fill-rule evenodd), transparent background, so Godot can tint them with modulate
grid.rule: the outer outline alone names the room (the 10 m case); counters and bubbles only confirm it up close (inner details of 9 units or more, up to about 5 m)
grid.face: faces/<id>.svg: 90 x 90 units = 0.45 m package face, 1 unit = 5 mm; a square ink frame of 4 units, a cream panel with radius 10, the 64-unit icon at 13..77, so the icon field is 0.32 m as in ground.md
grid.source: build.js writes every SVG from its geometry (node 20, no packages); edit the numbers there and rerun, never hand-edit the SVGs

rooms.silhouette: three solid crates in a stepped pyramid, no hand holes (separate blocks, unlike the one-block rack)
a station clock: a thick ring with the hands at three o'clock; the only hollow shape of the set
a chef's hat: a tall three-bump puff over a narrower band, taller than wide (46 x 57 units); no drink, so it stays apart from the lounge
a conical flask with a lipped neck and two bubbles; no cross or anything medical
a desk lamp: base, two arms, a head pointing down; the only zigzag of the set
a sofa: back, two arms, seat and legs; the widest, lowest shape (56 x 34 units)
a hammer and a spanner crossed: the only X
a solid upright rack on two feet: one block with three units, each a slot and a light

shared_files.plate.svg: the plate alone (frame and panel), for the door plate, the stand and the spot pad when the stamp is drawn on separately
shared_files.faces/: plate + stamp in one texture per room: what the package, the door plate, the stand and the pad import
shared_files.icons/: the stamp alone: the map tile and any 2D use

colours.introduced: none; two token colours carry the whole system

used.map: the existing map tokens only: map.room.panel (cream, ink 3 px, radius 12), map.board.panel (lavender), map.zone.panel (yellow, hover only)

contrast_wcag.tool: formulas of tools/a11y/contrast.js (ratio) and tools/a11y/cvd.js (Machado 2009 simulation, CIEDE2000), loaded unchanged in a scratch script since neither takes arguments
contrast_wcag.cream on lavender board: 1.19:1, never alone: the room tile's 3 px ink border separates them (12.13:1 and 14.37:1)
contrast_wcag.cream on zone yellow: 1.48:1, never alone: the same ink border

lit in 3D (light multiplies linear RGB b.note: door plates and stands go where the light is at least a quarter of full; tone mapping and exposure change the exact figures (unconfirmed)

package.what: the room's face tile on all six faces of the 0.45 m box. Adjacent faces' 4-unit frames meet at the edges as a 4 cm plum line, Toy's thick outline in 3D. The stamp field is 0.32 m: about 185 px when carried, 45 px at 5 m, 23 px at 10 m at 1080p (ground.md section 3). The top face matters most: the carrier sees it 35 degrees below the eye line.
package.godot: the package's existing MeshInstance3D with BoxMesh size 0.45; StandardMaterial3D: albedo_texture = faces/<id>.svg imported with svg/scale 4 (360 px), compress mode Lossless or VRAM Uncompressed, mipmaps on; uv1_scale = Vector3(3, 2, 1), which the BoxMesh reference gives for the same texture on every face (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.7/classes/class_boxmesh.html); texture_filter LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC; roughness 1 (matte, the non-glare finish of the US Access Board rules). Shaded like the scene: never unshaded or emissive.
package.check_in_godot: how BoxMesh orients each face's UVs is unconfirmed: the top face must read upright from the carrier and no face may be mirrored; if not, an ArrayMesh with its own UVs (tooling in prime-game)
package.vram: 360 x 360 RGBA with mipmaps is about 0.69 MB per room, about 4.1 MB for six destination rooms
package.not_used: Decal (would paint hands), Sprite3D billboard (floats like a marker), Label3D icon font (not needed: the texture stays sharp with mipmaps)

door.what: one 0.50 m square plate per door, 4 cm thick, ink body, the face tile on both sides (stamp field 0.36 m: about 25 px at 10 m and 17 px at 15 m at 1080p). A door on a corridor gets a projecting blade plate, perpendicular to the wall beside the latch side of the frame, bottom edge 2.0 m above the floor, so it reads from both ends of the corridor and over other players' heads. A door seen head-on across an open hall gets the same plate flush over the lintel. Nothing on the door leaf.
door.godot: a RoomSign scene: Node3D with a MeshInstance3D BoxMesh(0.5, 0.5, 0.04) in ink and two MeshInstance3D QuadMesh(0.5, 0.5), one per side, 1 mm proud, each with the face texture (two quads so neither side is mirrored). Depth test on, billboard off, no fixed_size.

map_room_tile.what: each room on the map is the existing map.room panel (cream, ink 3 px, radius 12) with its stamp, 32 px at the 1920 x 1080 base (21 px at 720p), above the room name (map.room-text, caption bold). Every room's stamp is shown all the time, at the same size. Hover-lit zones turn the tile zone yellow; the ink stamp stays 9.71:1.
map_room_tile.godot: PanelContainer with the map.room StyleBoxFlat > VBoxContainer > TextureRect (custom_minimum_size 32 x 32, expand_mode ignore size, stretch_mode STRETCH_KEEP_ASPECT_CENTERED; icons/<id>.svg as a DPITexture if #287 adopts it, else imported at svg/scale 1 (64 px) and drawn at 32) + Label

delivery_spot.what: the same in every room, only the stamp changes: a 1.2 m square cream pad with the face tile printed on it, and at its back edge a stand, an ink post with the door's 0.5 m plate centred 1.3 m above the floor, facing the room's main entrance. The stand reads from across the room; the pad confirms up close (a floor sign foreshortens, ground.md section 3). If a room has one spot for several packages (open question 1), the pad is 2.4 x 1.2 m with one stand.
delivery_spot.godot: a DeliverySpot scene: MeshInstance3D QuadMesh(1.2, 1.2) lying flat with the face texture (no Decal, so nothing else gets painted) + MeshInstance3D CylinderMesh post in ink + the RoomSign scene on top. The receiving area and its rules stay in #255's code.

placements.hud_hand_slot: proposal: no stamp in the slot; the box's top face already shows it at about 185 px while carried (open question 4 of ground.md, the engineer's call)

colour_blind.story: Nothing in A depends on hue. A room is told by its outline; the stamp and its plate are ink and cream, a lightness pair that every vision keeps apart. Packages stay colourless as decided.
colour_blind.weak_pairs: cream/lavender is 4.9 under tritan and 4.0 in greyscale, cream/zone 9.3 in greyscale (cvd.js thresholds: under 10 confusable); these are surfaces of the existing map tokens, always split by the room tile's ink border, and carry no room information

squint_test.method: squint check 2026-10-04 (scratch, not in the repo): each sign rasterised in headless Edge canvas at 24 px sharp, at 24 px with a Gaussian blur of sigma 1.5 px and at 16 px with sigma 1 px; distance = sum |a - b| / sum max(a, b) over the coverage masks (0 same, 1 no overlap); floor = a sign against itself shifted 1 px.

results.review pairs, 24 px blurred, before and: kitchen/lounge 0.417 to 0.575, storage/server 0.400 to 0.442, storage/lounge 0.413 to 0.574, kitchen/server 0.366 to 0.403

squint_test.changes_it_made: the hall clock became a ring (a solid disc was 0.283 from the chef's hat at 15 px; the ring lifts it off the closest list), and the rack was widened to 44 units (0.328 to 0.351 against the flask); after the 2026-10-04 review the crates lost their hand holes (a stepped pyramid), the rack became one upright block on feet, the hat taller and narrower and the sofa lower and wider
squint_test.limit: a pixel metric, not people: before the look is final, five people should name each stamp at a squint (ISO 9186-1 is the method for comprehension tests, https://www.iso.org/standard/59226.html)

not_a_destination_marker: Static: a stamp never glows, blinks, changes colour or plays a sound, whatever anyone carries; its materials are shaded, so in a dark corner it is as dim as the wall.
In the world only: depth-tested meshes, no billboard, no fixed_size, no no_depth_test; never on the HUD or at the screen edge.
The map shows every room's stamp all the time at one size; nothing on the map changes when a package is picked up.
A package shows one stamp, on its own faces only; the storage and hall stamps never appear on a package.
Rooms, not routes: no arrows; stamps only at doors, at spots and on the map.
At most three per room: one plate per door, the spot's stand and its pad.
Quieter than LOCKDOWN Protocol: one code instead of icon plus banner colour plus a light at the spot.
costs_and_risks: Cheapest system: 8 icons, 8 generated faces, one plate, two scenes (RoomSign, DeliverySpot) reused in every room, no new tokens.
It lives or dies by silhouettes: one code means no backup cue when a stamp is misread at 10 m or more; the player walks closer and the inner details settle it.
Rooms added later must pass the same squint test against all others before they ship.
BoxMesh face orientation is unconfirmed until tried in Godot.
Signs need light: at a tenth of full light the stamp drops to 2.7:1, so the level art keeps plates and stands lit.
